title: Land purchase for flood mitigation and Strong Mayors powers
subtitle: Mayor's decisions to keep current staff and committee practices, plus a moment of silence for a Cambridge councillor.
overview: Council held a short special meeting on August 14, 2023. The main decision was to acquire a set of properties totalling 2.575 acres, linked to the Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund. Council approved the purchase {{vote:m2}} after considering it in closed session, and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the documents to the City Solicitor's satisfaction.

The Mayor also told Council that Kitchener became subject to the Strong Mayors, Building Homes Act on July 1, 2023. The Mayor said that, through Mayoral Decisions, current practices would continue for hiring the Chief Administrative Officer, hiring the Corporate Leadership Team and setting up the standing committee structure. These decisions will be posted on a new section of the City's website.

Council opened with a moment of silence for Cambridge City Councillor Donna Reid. A Kitchener councillor declared a pecuniary interest on a closed-session fire station land matter and did not take part in it. The minutes report no public decision on that item. Council also confirmed its by-law and adjourned.

decisions.item: Land acquisition for Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund project
decisions.detail: Council approved acquiring three properties totalling 2.575 acres on the terms discussed in closed session, and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the documents {{vote:m2}}.

debate: On the Strong Mayors powers, the Mayor said the legislation is meant to help the province reach its housing targets and keep up the infrastructure that supports housing, including transit and servicing.
The Mayor said Council and staff have a collaborative relationship, so there was no reason to change how the CAO, department heads and committees are handled.
The Mayor said the CAO would keep a role in choosing department heads, and that committee set-up and chair appointments would continue as before.
For transparency, the Mayor said the decisions, and the by-laws once the Mayor has waived any veto, would be posted on a City web page.
The transcript has no debate on the land acquisition. The motion was moved, seconded and carried after the call for discussion.
